source.title: Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting in Incremental Few-Shot Learning by Finding Flat Minima
source.authors: Guangyuan Shi; Jiaxing Chen; Wenlong Zhang; Li-Ming Zhan; Xiao-Ming Wu

record.file_problem: not a file; supplied full paper text
record.tranche_reason: Uses flat-minima training as a method for incremental few-shot learning and reports its performance, but does not test the listed claims about natural-label generalization or the train-test gap.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses prior findings connecting flat minima and generalization, but does not test that relationship. Its own flatness measurements compare noise-based loss statistics for the Baseline and F2M; they are not magnitude-aware sharpness measures or measurements of a train-test gap.
record.test_reason: The study uses flat-minima training to mitigate catastrophic forgetting and evaluates its method's incremental few-shot classification performance. Its flatness statistics use absolute parameter perturbations and loss variation; they do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness, train–test generalization gaps, or rankings against norm- and margin-based measures. No other claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the conclusion: finding flat minima during base training and restricting later fine-tuning to that region can mitigate catastrophic forgetting in incremental few-shot learning. The authors suggest that limited capacity within the region may make the method unsuitable for medium- or high-shot tasks; this is a proposed limitation, not an experimentally demonstrated result.
record.recipe_differences: Incremental few-shot learning with flat-minima search and parameter clamping; not a study of the listed generalization claims.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured flatness statistics differ between the Baseline and F2M, and between training and testing sets.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 4 reports lower perturbed-loss variance for F2M than Baseline on training data (0.0506 versus 0.2993) and testing data (0.0800 versus 0.4582), and lower indicator I on both splits (0.0296 versus 0.1451; 0.0334 versus 0.2395).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training explicitly to find flat minima reduces absolute-noise loss-variation statistics relative to the baseline in this experiment.

record.problems: The flatness comparison is not a test of train-test-gap tracking; the reported statistics use noise perturbations and do not establish a correlation with generalization gap. Table 4 does not report uncertainty.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Width increases beyond zero training error and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness tracking train–test error gaps among similarly fitted networks, including comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All eight numerical values agree with Table 4. Their states remain cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, despite clear differences in the reported flatness statistics. The classification and ablation results concern incremental learning and do not supply missing tests of V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance under standard training.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization.
Batch size and the generalization gap under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and its effect on test accuracy.
